thread:
Maya: Quick thought — we should slim down the ingest interface for the observability pipeline to reduce cardinality and make cost attribution sane. The current envelope carries a lot of service-specific junk.
Sam: +1. Can we settle on a minimal envelope with required fields: trace_id, span_id, service, env, ts, payload_type, attrs (flat k/v)?
Maya: Yeah. attrs should be typed scalars only (string/number/bool). Drop blobs and arrays at ingest. Proposed header: ``ingest_schema_v`` and accept v1 (legacy) and v2 (canonical).
Tariq: Tradeoffs: less flexibility for ad-hoc fields, but we can have an `extensions` map with limits. Also, how do we propagate billing_key? If it lives in attrs it will explode cardinality.
Olivia: Suggest putting cost tags in a separate top-level `cost` object: {billing_key, project_id, allocation_fraction}. Billing_key should be hashed client-side or at ingest to reduce cardinality and privacy risk.
CI-bot: perf jobs will need updates. See job #632 for `ingest-schema` branch.
Jamal: Hashing SGTM. Also recommend server-side normalization & dedup early: normalize service names (lowercase, alias mapping), trim common prefixes. Keep mapping in config so we can iterate.
Maya: Implementation plan draft:
1) RFC + schema repo change (add v2 envelope)
2) Feature-flag `accept_ingest_v2` — accept v2 while also writing canonicalized events to a staging topic
3) Consumers adopt new fields (cost object + normalized service) and start reading staging topic
4) Backfill/migration window + cutover
Sam: Small enforcement rules: max_attrs=32, max_attr_key_len=64, and record a metric `ingest.attrs_dropped` with count and sample service. Drop extras with a well-defined behavior.
Tariq: Question: do we unify logs/traces/metrics envelopes? I'd prefer same top-level routing envelope but strict `payload_type` so downstream can multiplex.
Olivia: Also add a focused accuracy eval for cost attribution — baseline current vs new approach for 2 weeks. If discrepancy >2% we iterate before full cutover.
Maya: I'll draft the RFC today with an example envelope and a backwards-compat plan. Will call out rollout gates (cardinality, cost regression, perf).
Sam: :thumbsup: I'll take perf/ingest infra changes (staging topic, runner changes, enforce limits).
Jamal: I'll own the normalization map and start compiling known service aliases.
CI-bot: CI job #632 queued by Sam — ETA ~45m.
Maya: Example minimal envelope (proto-ish):
```
{
  "ingest_schema_v": 2,
  "trace_id": "...",
  "span_id": "...",
  "service": "redwood-ingest",
  "env": "prod",
  "ts": "2026-03-20T15:12:00Z",
  "payload_type": "trace/span",
  "cost": {"billing_key_hash":"sha256:abcd...","project_id":"p-123","allocation_fraction":0.75},
  "attrs": {"http.status_code":200, "user_tier":"enterprise"},
  "extensions": {"legacy": "raw_payload_id"}
}
```
Maya: Open questions for RFC reviewers:
- hashing strategy for billing_key (client vs ingest)
- limits for `extensions` (size + sampling)
- migration window length (2–4 weeks?)
- metrics to gate cutover (attrs_dropped, unique_billing_keys, ingest_p99)
Sam: I can prepare perf benchmarks for current vs v2 (ingest latency and storage delta) once RFC lands.
Tariq: We'll also need a quick migration job template to backfill normalized service names for historical data in small batches.
Olivia: Tagging product for visibility on cost attribution changes — ping them after RFC: @product.
Maya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link in this thread when ready. If you want to be a reviewer, ping me here.
Sam: I'll review tonight.
Jamal: Will add initial alias list into `ingest-normalization` repo.
